body: Thanks! clangd really likes trolling me by including stuff.

CodeEdit shouldn't have color picker, especially since it isn't even available for regular CodeEdits (and it doesn't need to be exposed either).
I actually moved the color picker out of the individual text editors, so they all share one in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/115662
Exposing these doesn't make sense, they can't be used,
We should probably expose these as Inlay Hints `inlay_hints` instead, to match other IDEs (none that I tested use `inline`).

:thinking:  I see the changes you made and it makes sense to have one centralized color picker. But I'd still argue that the actual color hint, should be handled by `CodeEdit`, and inlay-hint functionality should be exposed.
True, currently they cannot be used, but as said in my previous comment, I think that the inlay-hint functionality should be exposed, and thus the theming that goes with it.

I agree that they should be exposed, but they need to be refactored first (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/108822) and I don't know when that will happen, so we shouldn't expose anything until then.

I don't see why CodeEdit should handle color hints. 
The parsing logic is language specific and doesn't make sense for all languages. CodeEdit is general purpose, having color hints or even just a color picker on it does not suit it.
Once inlay hints are exposed, users can add color pickers on their own, and they probably will want to customize it. The current implementation is very opinionated since it has an option button injected into the default ColorPicker, so users will have to keep that in mind.
It shouldn't be too much effort to implement it either once the inlay hints are exposed, so its not saving users much time.
